question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 4}\frac{{y}^{2}-16}{{y}^{2}-4y} & =\frac{(4)^{2}-16}{(4)^{2}-4(4)} \\  & =\frac{16-16}{16-16} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}-16}{{y}^{2}-4y} & =\frac{(y-4)(y+4)}{y(y-4)} \\  & =\frac{y+4}{y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{y\to 4}\frac{{y}^{2}-16}{{y}^{2}-4y} & ={lim}_{y\to 4}\frac{y+4}{y} \\  & =\frac{4+4}{4} \\  & =\frac{8}{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
